name: TripoSplat
description: Single image to 3D via feed-forward Gaussian Splatting (up to 262k Gaussians). The Generate node reconstructs a vertex-colored mesh; the Texture node smooths it and bakes the color into a UV texture atlas. By Tripo AI / VAST AI Research. Requires ~10GB VRAM.
author: Lorchie

params_schema.label: Sampling Steps
params_schema.tooltip: Number of diffusion sampling steps. More steps = cleaner Gaussians but slower.

params_schema.label: CFG Scale
params_schema.tooltip: Classifier-free guidance strength. Higher = closer to the input image.

params_schema.label: Detail / Shape (Shift)
params_schema.tooltip: Flow schedule shift. 1.0 = uniform; higher spends more steps on the high-noise (global shape) end. Affects detail vs overall form.

params_schema.label: Gaussians
params_schema.tooltip: Number of Gaussians to decode. More = denser point cloud and finer mesh detail.

params_schema.label: Mesh Detail
params_schema.tooltip: Poisson reconstruction depth. Higher = sharper geometry but slower and more triangles (and more noise to smooth in the Texture node).

params_schema.label: Edge Cleanup
params_schema.tooltip: Pixels eroded from the background-removal mask before compositing. Higher removes more edge halo/bleed around the subject. 0 disables.

params_schema.label: Seed
params_schema.tooltip: Seed for reproducibility. Set to -1 for a random seed.

params_schema.label: Surface Smoothing
params_schema.tooltip: Taubin smoothing strength (volume-preserving). Removes the Poisson orange-peel. Strong = very smooth but loses fine detail.

params_schema.label: UV Quality
params_schema.tooltip: UV unwrap method for the texture bake. Voronoi packs fewer seams but needs a clean manifold mesh (auto-falls back to Trivial).

params_schema.label: Texture Size
params_schema.tooltip: Resolution of the baked color texture atlas. Higher = sharper surface color but larger file.

params_schema.label: Max Faces
params_schema.tooltip: Target face count after smoothing (quadric decimation). -1 to keep full density.
